title: Cubans in Florida waver on Trump and Republicans over immigration
summary:
Since the Trump administration launched its crackdown on undocumented immigrants two years ago, the waiting room of Cuban-born immigration lawyer, Ismael Labrador, in Miami is never empty.
Cubans have traditionally enjoyed favoured immigration status in the United States under provisions enshrined in 1960s-era legislation called the Cuban Adjustment Act.
"The way I put it is that if you don't have a Green Card in the United States, you may be a target."
Despite his best efforts, the immigration lawyer was unable to prevent his own relative from being deported back to Cuba.
ICE, meanwhile, has said it is targeting anyone who has broken American immigration law and is in the country illegally.

title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain
summary:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to announce her final decision on immigration rules for legal migrants next week.
She had proposed to extend the wait for permanent settlement from the current five years to 10 with some lower-paid migrants facing a 15-year wait.
The BBC understands the proposals are likely to be revised for most of those currently working in social care.
Mahmood has faced opposition from within the government for proposing to impose new rules on migrant workers already in the UK.
In particular, many lower-paid social care workers were facing a wait of up to 15 years rather than five.

title: A Refugee City Plan Refuses to Treat Shelter as Enough
summary:
Six family plots sharing a courtyard is a modest starting point for an ambitious city plan.
BIG, short for Bjarke Ingels Group, lists the architectural project as Refugee Future Cities, with a masterplan for Bidi Bidi in northern Uganda.
Designer: BIG (Bjarke Ingels Group)The plan grows outward from family plots into compounds, clusters, and neighborhoods.
That arrangement makes sense to me because a city needs intermediate spaces between a private home and a public street.
The first planned physical step is a single-family base prototype at the Bidi Bidi Performing Arts Centre.

title: ICE activity is surging ahead of midterms. So is voter turnout.
summary:
ICE activity is surging ahead of midterms.
In the weeks ahead of the midterms, various cities and states across the country are reporting a notable rise in ICE activity, according to reports gathered by NPR and its member stations.
An official within New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office who was not authorized to speak publicly confirmed that they have noted a surge in ICE activity in the city.
"What we were seeing in early October and what we've seen continue, at least anecdotally throughout this month, is that ICE activity has really picked up in Portland."
"I'd say it's a noticeable uptick compared to what we've seen over the summer."

title: Democrats are the unwitting beneficiaries of Trump’s immigration policies
summary:
In a recent Fox News poll, most Americans believe the Trump administration has “gone too far” in enforcing immigration laws, including 60% of independents.
On inflation, the economy and foreign policy, his net approval rating is at negative 42.8%, negative 31.7% and negative 27.8%, respectively.
According to The Economist/YouGov polling cited earlier, 1% of Democrats named immigration as their top issue in September 2026.
Remarkably, without Democrats’ endorsement of a single new immigration policy idea, independents now express greater trust in Democrats than Republicans on immigration, 41% to 27%, according to a September 2026 Marist survey.
After the global pandemic halted most human mobility in 2020, the Biden administration sought to avoid the immigration issue altogether.

title: Indicted ICE officer accused of intentionally striking man expected to surrender on Monday
summary:
The Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer accused of intentionally striking a man in Houston earlier this month is expected to surrender on Monday morning, his attorney, David Lindenmuth told ABC News.
Mario Alberto Morales was indicted by a grand jury in Houston on a charge of second-degree aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, according to the Harris County District Attorney's Office.
Authorities say that’s when the vehicle struck Parra Hernandez and then came to a stop.
According to Lindenmuth, Morales is a former corrections officer who enlisted in the Army.
Morales also worked as a detention and processing officer at the Port Isabel Detention Center and worked with DHS as an ICE contractor, Lindenmuth said.

title: DHS Citizenship Agency Reverses Biden Giveaways to 2.2 Million Migrants
summary:
A little-known agency within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has ended a myriad legal giveaways to 2.2 million migrants welcomed by President Joe Biden.
Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) agency is “reversing the downstream effects of the Biden border crisis,” the department stated on October 29.
Under Biden, the agency served as a rubber stamp for illegal migrants, criminals, low-wage employers, and the Democratic Party’s urban machines.
The legal process canceled their work permits and allows ICE to fly them back home to Haiti.
USCIS has also revived security reviews and fact checks when awarding migration benefits, including work permits, work visas, green cards, and citizenship.

title: Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer accused of running over man in Houston
summary:
Share Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer accused of running over man in Houston on social mediaA grand jury in Texas has indicted a United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer accused of deliberately running over a Mexican construction worker during an operation in Houston this month.
ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales faces charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon for the October 10 incident, Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare announced on Friday.
Criminal charges against federal immigration officers have been rare during President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, although several encounters involving officers have prompted investigations.
Teare also accused federal authorities of failing to cooperate with the investigation, including by removing the Jeep before local investigators could examine it for potential evidence.
An ICE officer, Gregory Feathers, has been accused of firing at the vehicle Salgado Araujo was driving on his way to work in Houston.
